title: Protocol for establishing organoids from human ovarian cancer biopsies
protocol: Collect OC tissue biopsy in a conical tube with 10 mL collection medium on ice and process immediately.
Transfer the tissue to a Petri dish in the biological safety cabinet.
Rinse the tissue extensively with 5 mL PBS using a plastic transfer pipet to wash away blood and FBS.
Repeat rinsing until the PBS becomes clear.
Split the tumor biopsy into three parts for cryopreservation, fixation/histology, and organoid formation.
Transfer tissue in collection medium to a Petri dish.
Rinse the biopsy multiple times with PBS.
Cut the biopsy into small pieces using a scalpel.
Incubate the tissue piece (∼4 mm3) in 3 mL of 4% PFA for 15–20 hours on ice.
Remove the PFA from the tube.
Add 5 mL PBS to rinse the sample and place the tube on a shaking plate with mild shaking for 15 minutes.
Remove the PBS.
Repeat steps e to g twice.
Add 2 mL of Ethanol 70% to the tissue.
Store the tissue in EtOH 70% at 4°C until further processing (not longer than 6 months).
Mince the rest of the biopsy into small pieces using a scalpel (pieces of 1–2 mm3).
Rinse the minced tissue repeatedly with 3 mL PBS until the fluid becomes clear.
Add 1 mL of cryopreservation medium to one cryovial.
Add approximately 10 pieces of tissue per vial and keep on ice.
Place the cryovials in a cryobox as soon as possible and freeze at −80°C for 15–20 hours.
Transfer the cryovials to liquid nitrogen for long-term storage the following day.
Collect all remaining tissue pieces into a 30 mL conical tube with 8 mL dissociation medium.
Incubate the tube in a 37°C water bath for 1–2 hours.
Mechanically assist enzymatic dissociation by pipetting the sample up and down every 20 minutes using a glass Pasteur pipet.
Further dissociate clumps every 20 minutes using a fire-polished Pasteur pipet narrowed to about half its original diameter.
Add 50 μL DNase (0.2 mg/mL) to the suspension and incubate for 1 minute at 20°C–22°C.
Stop enzymatic activity by adding ice-cold 8 mL DMEM/F12 + 10% FBS.
Filter the solution through a 70 μm cell strainer to collect dissociated cells, discarding any large tissue fragments that remain on the strainer.
Centrifuge the filtered suspension at 220 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant from the cell pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL DMEM/F12 at 20°C–22°C and transfer to an Eppendorf tube.
Centrifuge the suspension at 220 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet in 500 μL DMEM/F12 at 20°C–22°C.
Count cells using an automated cell counter or hemocytometer, ignoring small clumps.
Calculate the number of wells that can be plated with 30,000 cells per well.
Take off the correct amount of supernatant and resuspend the pellet in ice-cold Matrigel to achieve a ratio of 70% Matrigel/30% cell suspension (in DMEM/F12).
Mix slowly to avoid air bubbles.
Dispense 20 μL droplets per well in a pre-warmed 48-well culture plate, ensuring the Matrigel is liquid.
Place the plate upside down in the 37°C/5% CO2 incubator for 20 min to allow Matrigel solidification and cell distribution.
Prewarm OCOM in a 37°C water bath.
Add RI (10 μM) to the medium.
Add 250 μL warm OCOM to each well.
Return the plate to the 37°C/5% CO2 incubator.
Refresh the culture medium every 2–3 days without RI.
Passage organoids when they reach a diameter of around 200–300 μm and appropriate confluency.
Remove the medium from the wells containing organoids ready for passage.
Add 400 μL of ice-cold DMEM/F12 per well.
Pipette up and down multiple times with a p1000 tip to release organoids from Matrigel.
Gently scratch the bottom of the well with the pipette tip to aid detachment.
Transfer 400 μL from the first well to subsequent wells for pooled samples.
Collect resuspended organoids in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube and place on ice.
Rinse all collected wells once with 400 μL DMEM/F12.
Double-check under light microscope to ensure all organoids are collected.
Repeat rinsing if necessary.
Centrifuge at 220 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Prewarm an aliquot of TrypLE Express (supplemented with RI at 10 μM) in a 37°C water bath.
Remove supernatant from pelleted organoids.
Add 500 μL prewarmed TrypLE to each Eppendorf tube containing the organoid pellet.
Swirl tubes gently to mix organoids with TrypLE.
Incubate in a 37°C water bath for 10 min (dense organoids) or 5 min (low-cohesive and cystic organoids).
Add 500 μL ice-cold DMEM/F12 to each tube to inactivate TrypLE activity.
Centrifuge at 220 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the organoid pellet in 700 μL ice-cold DMEM/F12.
Place a P200 tip over a P1000 tip and pipet up and down for 25 times to mechanically disrupt the organoids.
Centrifuge at 220 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet in 500 μL DMEM/F12.
Count the cells using an automated cell counter or hemocytometer.
Calculate the number of wells that can be plated and the amount of cell suspension and Matrigel needed.
Resuspend the pellet in 70% Matrigel and keep on ice.
Dispense 20 μL droplets, containing 30,000 cells per well, in a pre-warmed 48-well culture plate.
Incubate the plate upside down in the 37°C/5% CO2 incubator for 20 min.
Pre-warm OCOM in a 37°C water bath.
Add RI (10 μM) to the medium.
Add 250 μL warm OCOM to each well.
Return the plate to the 37°C/5% CO2 incubator.
Refresh the culture medium every 2–3 days.
Passage the organoids again at confluence (every 14–28 days).
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL cryopreservation medium after centrifugation.
Transfer the resuspended sample into a cryovial and place on ice.
Place the cryovials containing organoids from 1 to 4 confluent wells in a cryobox.
Transfer the cryobox to −80°C.
The next day, transfer samples to liquid nitrogen for long-term storage.
Remove the cryovial from liquid nitrogen and put on ice.
Thaw the solution with cryopreserved OC organoids in a 37°C water bath for maximum 2 minutes.
Transfer the thawed content to a 15 mL conical tube with ice-cold 10 mL DMEM/F12/10% FBS.
Rinse the cryovial with 1 mL DMEM F12/10% FBS.
Centrifuge at 220 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet with 1 mL ice-cold DMEM/F12.
Transfer the suspension to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Centrifuge at 220 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet in 500 μL ice-cold DMEM/F12.
Count the cells using an automated cell counter or hemocytometer.
Calculate the number of wells that can be plated and the amount of cell suspension and Matrigel needed.
Resuspend the pellet in 70% Matrigel and keep on ice.
Dispense 20 μL droplets containing 30,000 cells per well in a pre-warmed 48-well culture plate.
Incubate the plate upside down in the 37°C/5% CO2 incubator for 20 min.
Pre-warm OCOM in a 37°C water bath.
Add RI (10 μM) to the medium.
Add 250 μL warm OCOM to each well and return the plate to the 37°C/5% CO2 incubator.
Refresh the culture medium every 2–3 days.
Passage the organoids again at confluence (i.e., every 14–28 days).
Remove the medium from the wells with organoids that need to be analyzed.
Add 400 μL of ice-cold DMEM/F12 to the well.
Pipette up and down multiple times with a p1000 tip to release the organoids from the Matrigel.
Collect the organoids in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube and put on ice.
Centrifuge at 220 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant containing the Matrigel.
Resuspend the organoid pellet in 1 mL of 4% PFA in the chemical hood.
Incubate for 1 h at 20°C–22°C.
Centrifuge at 220 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Wash by resuspending the pellet in 1 mL PBS and centrifuging at 200 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Repeat washing step twice more.
Resuspend the final pellet in 1 mL of EtOH 70%.
Store organoids in EtOH 70% at 4°C for up to 1 month.
Pellet the PFA-fixed organoids in 70% EtOH at 220 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant and resuspend pellet in 1 mL of 100% EtOh using a plastic transfer pipet.
Label glass flat-bottom tubes with tape to avoid wiping out with EtOH.
Fill the labeled flat-bottom tubes with approximately 4 mL of 100% EtOh.
Transfer organoids into the flat-bottom tube containing 100% EtOh and pipette up and down a few times.
Wash the Eppendorf tube with 100% EtOh to ensure all organoids are transferred.
Let the organoids settle by gravity for 30 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Discard most of the 100% EtOH and rinse again with 100% EtOH.
Pipette up and down when adding the EtOH to mix the solution thoroughly.
Let the organoids settle again for 30 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Repeat washing steps using 100% EtOH once.
Rinse the organoids with N-Butanol and let them settle for 30 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Perform two more washing steps of 30 minutes each with N-Butanol.
Remove as much N-Butanol as possible from the organoids.
Pre-warm the heating block in the paraffin solution of the HistoStar Embedding Workstation.
Resuspend the organoids in warm paraffin solution and incubate for 30 minutes at 60°C.
Discard three-quarters of the paraffin, allowing the organoids to settle at the bottom of the tube.
Light up a cartridge burner to warm a metal mold and keep it warm in the HistoStar.
Warm a glass Pasteur pipet with the cartridge burner.
Transfer rapidly all organoids in melted paraffin from the glass tube to the warmed metal mold using the pipet.
Move all the organoids to the center of the metal mold with blunt forceps.
Place the metal mold on a cold plate of the HistoStar for 10 seconds.
Put the cassette on the metal mold and cover it with warm paraffin from Histostar.
Let it cool down for 20 minutes on the cold plate.
Remove the metal mold and store the paraffin blocks at 4°C until further processing.
Calculate the number of wells that can be plated with 2,000 cells per 3 μL droplet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 70% Matrigel and keep it on ice.
Dispense one 3 μL droplet containing approximately 2,000 cells per well in a pre-warmed 96-well flat-bottom culture plate.
Incubate the plate upside down in the 37°C/5% CO2 incubator for 10 minutes.
Pre-warm OCOM in a 37°C water bath.
Add RI (10 μM) to the medium.
Add 100 μL of warm OCOM to each well and return the plate to the 37°C/5% CO2 incubator.
Refresh the culture medium every 2–3 days and allow organoids to form for 2–4 weeks.
Apply a concentration dilution series of tested drugs or control (vehicle) to the organoid cultures in triplicate wells.
Refresh the drug at the tested dilutions after 48 hours.
Assess cell viability after 72 hours of drug treatment using the XTT assay.
Prepare 1 mg/mL XTT labeling mixture by dissolving XTT powder in DMEM/F12 and adding 1/1000 electron-coupling reagent PMS.
Pre-warm the mixture for 30 minutes in a 37°C water bath, vortexing every 10 minutes.
Add 100 μL XTT labeling mixture per organoid well.
Incubate at 37°C/5% CO2 for 4 hours.
Measure the absorbance of the samples using a microplate reader at 450 nm.
